items.t: Petrobras Plans November Diesel Imports as Refineries Run Near Capacity
sum: Petrobras will bring in 600 million litres of diesel during November to rebuild inventories drawn down by scheduled maintenance at its refineries, the company said. The volume works out to roughly 125,000 barrels per day and follows work at the RNEST and Repar units.

That figure sits below October's 650 million litres, even as the state-controlled producer restocks tanks emptied during the turnarounds. Angélica Laureano, Petrobras's director for logistics, marketing and markets, set out the import plan in remarks carried by media outlets.

Processing rates are not easing. Refineries ran at 98% of capacity in October, and director William Franca has signalled that November and December should stay close to the operational ceiling, Reuters reported on 30 October. December will also bring a shift in the product slate: more gasoline to meet summer demand, less diesel once the planting season winds down. The plants themselves remain heavily loaded while that mix changes.

Those maintenance-driven imports sit alongside a production performance that set new highs. Petrobras lifted 3.51 million barrels of oil equivalent per day of oil, gas and natural gas liquids in the third quarter of 2026 — a company record and 11.7% more than a year earlier. Exports of crude and refined products also peaked, at 1.25 million barrels per day.

Not every project is running to schedule. First gas at Sirius, the offshore venture shared with Ecopetrol, has slipped from 2030 to 2031. Alcindo Mortiz, who heads Petrobras Colombia, attributed the delay to difficulties in the consultation process. On the exploration front, the company confirmed a third oil find at the Morpho well in block FZA-M-59, located in the Foz do Amazonas basin, on 29 October.

The trading backdrop has turned less friendly. Brent was heading for a weekly loss of 16%, with results from the US midterm elections fuelling hopes of a de-escalation in the US-Israeli war against Iran and of additional crude flowing out of the Middle East. Continued attacks on tankers, meanwhile, provided a counterweight that kept a floor under prices.
Petrobras stock came under pressure on Wednesday alongside other Brazilian oil producers as crude fell sharply. On Friday the shares shed 1.9% to close at €7.67.

Petrobras stock: RINA wins USD 12.3 million subsea contract
sum: RINA has secured a three-year contract worth USD 12.3 million from Petrobras for engineering and technical assessments of subsea infrastructure in Brazil, according to AD HOC NEWS, citing Offshore Engineer. The announcement adds a new operational detail to Petrobras' recent production-led investment case.

The assignment covers the integrity and reliability of subsea pipelines and risers, maintenance planning, technical studies for decommissioning and options to extend the operating life of offshore assets. RINA will also examine intervention scenarios across the lifecycle of subsea systems.

The scope includes FMEA and FMECA reliability studies, RAM analyses, asset-life evaluations and technical work for subsea decommissioning. RINA said the project can mobilize up to 83 engineers and specialized technicians, including about 45 specialists already employed by the company.

The contract concerns offshore asset integrity and lifecycle management rather than a disclosed production increase or financial target. Its direct earnings contribution was not specified, so the immediate investor relevance lies in maintenance planning, operating-life decisions and decommissioning preparation across Petrobras' offshore portfolio.

Petrobras to Report Q3 Earnings: What's in the Cards for the Stock?
sum: Petróleo Brasileiro S.A. - Petrobras PBR is set to release third-quarter 2026 results on Nov. 10. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for earnings is pegged at $1.23 per share on revenues of $31.3 billion.

Let us delve into the factors that are likely to have influenced the integrated oil and gas firm's performance in the to-be-reported quarter. But it is worth taking a look at PBR's previous-quarter performance first.

In the last reported quarter, the Rio de Janeiro-based Brazilian state-run energy giant beat the consensus mark, driven by strong production, exports and Brent pricing. Petrobras reported adjusted earnings per ADS of $1.72, which beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $1.52. Moreover, the company's quarterly revenues of $33.6 billion surpassed the consensus estimate of $30.8 billion.
PBR's earnings beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate in three of the last four quarters and missed in one, resulting in a surprise of 3%, on average. This is depicted in the graph below:
Petroleo Brasileiro S.A.- Petrobras price-eps-surprise | Petroleo Brasileiro S.A.- Petrobras Quote

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for the third-quarter bottom line has been revised 1.7% upward in the past 30 days. The estimated figure indicates 50% year-over-year growth. The consensus estimate for revenues also indicates growth of 33.3% from the year-ago period.

Petrobras appears well positioned for a third-quarter 2026 earnings beat, supported by record production and stronger refined-product sales. Per the press release on Oct. 28, the company's own total oil and gas output rose 11.7% year over year and 5.3% sequentially to 3.51 million barrels of oil equivalent per day, benefiting from the ramp-up of P-78 and P-79, higher output at Mero and fewer maintenance-related losses. Domestic refined-product sales increased 6.4% sequentially to 1.85 million barrels per day, led by diesel and jet fuel demand. Refinery utilization remained high at 99%, while diesel production hit a quarterly record of 769,000 barrels per day. Record oil and product exports of 1.25 million barrels per day, supported by logistics improvements, further strengthen the revenue outlook.

Petrobras stock hits record Q3 output as new platforms ramp up
sum: Petrobras set a production record in the third quarter of 2026 as new offshore platforms and higher operating efficiency lifted output. The companys own production of oil, natural gas liquids and natural gas averaged 3.512 million barrels of oil equivalent per day, according to World Oil on October 29.

The quarterly average rose 5.3 percent from the second quarter and 11.7 percent from a year earlier. Petrobras attributed the increase to its highest production efficiency in eight years, the ramp-up of the P-78 and P-79 floating production, storage and offloading units at Búzios, peak output from the Alexandre de Gusmão platform at Mero and fewer losses from maintenance shutdowns.

Twelve new producing wells started during the quarter, six in the Campos basin and six in the Santos basin. Total operated production, including volumes attributable to partners, reached a record 5.08 million barrels of oil equivalent per day, while operated pre-salt production climbed to 4.46 million.

Petrobras own pre-salt oil production rose 6.7 percent from the previous quarter to 2.454 million barrels per day. The increase was supported by seven new wells, six of them in Santos. Production from post-salt deep and ultra-deep fields fell 4.2 percent to 341,000 barrels per day because of maintenance losses in Campos and natural decline at mature fields.

At Mero, the Alexandre de Gusmão platform reached its design capacity of 180,000 barrels per day in August and hit a peak of 190,000 barrels per day in September after a capacity increase was approved. The Sepetiba platform reached a daily peak of 212,000 barrels, while Mero platforms averaged 760,000 barrels per day during the quarter.

The Almirante Tamandaré platform at Búzios recorded a monthly peak of 263,000 barrels per day in July. Petrobras said the P-80 and P-82 platforms left a Singapore shipyard in late September and mid-October for Búzios. Each platform is designed to produce 225,000 barrels per day and is scheduled to start up in 2027.

Chief exploration and production officer Sylvia Anjos said the company was producing more and using its assets more effectively, supported by operational excellence, safety and technology. The associated gas utilization index reached a record 98.3 percent.

Brazilian Stocks Tumble as Lula Wins Surprise Fourth Term: Nu Holdings Sinks 25%, Petrobras Slides 21%, MercadoLibre Drops 15%
sum: Lula's surprise return to Brazil's presidency blindsided investors who had positioned for the opposite outcome, and the fallout is carving deep losses into some of the most widely held Brazilian names trading in the U.S.

Brazil’s surprise election result is hitting the country’s U.S.-listed companies hardest where government policy and borrowing costs carry the most weight. Nu Holdings (NYSE:NU | NU Price Prediction) stock is down 25% to $11.30 in morning trading, a drop that marks the market’s toughest verdict on Brazil’s financial-services outlook.

Meanwhile, Petrobras (NYSE:PBR) stock is sliding 21% to $20.54, trailing only Nu Holdings among the three companies, as the state-controlled oil producer faces fresh questions about government influence. MercadoLibre (NASDAQ:MELI) shares are falling 15% to $1,545, a smaller decline than either Nu Holdings or Petrobras.

The selling pressure is landing directly on Brazil. Tracking a broad basket of Brazilian equities, the iShares MSCI Brazil ETF (NYSEARCA:EWZ) is down 28% to $30.66, a deeper slide than any of the three companies. For comparison, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA:SPY) is up 0.3% to $762.13, showing that risk appetite outside of Brazil is holding steady.

Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won Brazil’s presidential runoff over the weekend, a surprise victory that gives him a fourth term and sends a shock through Nu Holdings, Petrobras and MercadoLibre shares. Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, who led the first round earlier this month, has refused to concede, adding further political uncertainty.

Investors had largely positioned for a Bolsonaro win and the economic reforms it was expected to bring. Brazil is dealing with deteriorating public finances and elevated interest rates. Whether Lula’s more gradual approach to fiscal repair can still bring borrowing costs down is now the central question hanging over Brazilian assets.

Nu Holdings is a digital financial services platform operating primarily in Brazil, Mexico and Colombia, with the majority of its customers in Brazil. That footprint ties the company directly to Brazilian interest rates, consumer credit conditions and the tax treatment of financial services.

items.t: Petrobras PBR Stock Surges as Bolsonaro Election and Oil Discovery Drive Rally
sum: Petrobras shares surged to their highest level in more than a decade, but the sharp rally now faces political and valuation risks.
- Petrobras shares surged 12% in pre-market trading, reaching their highest level since 2012 following Brazil's first-round presidential election.
- The stock rally is attributed to right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro's unexpected strong performance, securing 47% of the vote.
- Renewed optimism around Petrobras' exploration portfolio, particularly after a second oil discovery at the Morpho well, has bolstered investor sentiment.
- Despite the surge, analysts caution that political and valuation risks may impact the stock's ability to maintain its breakout.

Petrobras stock surged 12% in pre-market trading to nearly $25, reaching its highest level since 2012 as U.S.-listed Brazilian shares rallied following Brazil’s first-round presidential election. The move reflects a sharp shift in investor sentiment after right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro outperformed expectations and secured 47% of the vote.

Bolsonaro will face President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva in a runoff later this month after Lula received roughly 45%. Polls had expected Lula to finish ahead, making the result a significant political surprise for investors.

Petrobras registered strong buying interest following the announcement of a second crude oil discovery at the ultra-deepwater Morpho exploratory well in the Foz do Amazonas basin. Located in the strategic Equatorial Margin off the coast of Amapá state, this new oil-bearing interval confirms high-quality crude reserves and significantly enhances confidence in Brazil's frontier exploration potential. The successful drilling campaign reinforces Petrobras's long-term reserve replacement capability, mitigating market concerns over production depletion while validating management's strategic focus on offshore growth assets.

Underpinning this operational optimism, Petrobras confirmed key advances in its core pre-salt asset base as the massive P-80 floating production, storage, and offloading vessel departed for the flagship Búzios field. Designed to add substantial daily crude oil production capacity, the platform's transit signals that medium-term volume expansion plans remain on schedule. Simultaneously, investor sentiment was supported by the steady receipt of government fuel subvention payments, which continue to bolster balance sheet liquidity and provide cash flow predictability amidst evolving domestic fuel pricing policies.

From a macro and sector perspective, Petrobras continues to demonstrate strong relative resilience despite intraday price swings across global crude benchmarks. The company's combination of low pre-salt lifting costs, robust free cash flow generation, and generous shareholder return policies continues to attract institutional capital. While broader energy market volatility persists due to global supply crosscurrents, Petrobras's operational execution and expanded reserve horizon helped the equity post gains and outpace broader industry indexes.

MAJURO, Marshall Islands, Oct. 01, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Remittix has scheduled the RTX token launch for November 24, 2026, establishing a public-market date after surpassing $32 million in presale funding. More than 40,000 participants have joined the project, which is now progressing toward a $36 million hard cap and the final integration of its PayFi, wallet, trading and earning products.

The announcement coincides with two examples of blockchain moving into real-world operations. The Cardano Foundation and Petrobras have advanced fuel-tracing applications, while NEAR Intents has detailed how its SHIELD system responded to swaps connected with the Bitget hack.
The confirmed date turns Remittix’s remaining presale period into a defined countdown. RTX is currently available at $0.21, while $0.46 has been announced as the price of the final presale stage.

Remittix is developing crypto-to-bank infrastructure aimed at one of digital assets’ most persistent usability problems: converting cryptocurrency into spendable fiat without requiring users to navigate multiple exchanges, wallets and withdrawal processes. The PayFi platform is designed to send supported crypto and settle the value into compatible bank accounts.

The project has opened testing to an initial 1,000 users. The Remittix Wallet is already live on iOS with more than 10,000 downloads, its Remittix Markets platform has processed over $50 million in perpetual-futures volume, and Remittix Earn is approaching release with advertised yields of up to 22% APY on selected holdings.

The Cardano Foundation has announced two research initiatives with Petrobras, Brazil’s state-controlled energy company. One uses Cardano to create verifiable records for sustainable aviation fuel environmental claims, helping prevent the same emissions benefit from being counted more than once.

Braskem seeks restructuring of $10.9bn debt
sum: Petrochemical producer wins 90-day standstill after securing support from holders of 39.6% of debt covered by proceeding

Braskem, one of the world’s ten largest petrochemical companies, filed Monday (24) for court approval of an out-of-court restructuring aimed at overhauling $10.9 billion in financial debt, equivalent to R$56.5 billion at current exchange rates.

Talks between the company and creditors stretched into Sunday night as a 60-day injunction protecting Braskem from debt collection and enforcement actions approached its expiration. The filing gives the petrochemical producer more time to develop a plan capable of winning support from a majority of the claims included in the restructuring.

Braskem has secured backing from holders of 39.6% of the financial debt covered by the proceeding, although that does not mean creditors have agreed to all terms of a potential restructuring. As Valor reported, there is still no formal written plan, despite progress on some issues. The company will use the next 90 days to flesh out the proposal and seek the required support of more than 50% of the claims.

Although the out-of-court restructuring filing had been widely expected, Braskem shares fell 6.7% on B3 to R$4.73 on Monday, their lowest level in 17 years. Following the filing, B3 removed the stock from its indices.
One of the commitments reached so far calls for controlling shareholders IG4 Capital and state-controlled oil company Petrobras to provide funding if certain milestones are not met.

In that context, one option under discussion is for Braskem to tap the capital markets in the future if its financial metrics deteriorate, people familiar with the negotiations said. A follow-on share offering, potentially open to the controlling and minority shareholders as well, is the majority shareholders’ preferred route for raising capital.

What a Flávio Bolsonaro victory could mean for Brazil’s oil and gas sector
sum: A possible victory by Flávio Bolsonaro in Brazil's October 2026 presidential elections could reverse part of the reorientation promoted by Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva at Petrobras, with more room for private capital in the oil and gas sector and a possible resumption of divestments by the state-run firm.

The oil company is not mentioned in the government plan of the candidate from the Liberal Party (PL), while in the Workers’ Party candidate’s program it appears as a central agent of national energy development – which has not had a large public electric utility since the privatization of Eletrobras in 2022.

Flávio Bolsonaro even went so far as to advocate for the privatization of Petrobras that year, when his father, Jair Bolsonaro – then president of the republic – authorized the start of studies for the company’s privatization. In 2026, however, the candidate mentioned that only some companies and assets within Petrobras could be sold.

This would already represent an important change in relation to Lula, who, right at the beginning of his government in 2023, suspended Petrobras’ divestment program, which included the sale of eight refineries – four of which were sold under Jair’s administration.
Lula also directed Petrobras to resume investments in expanding its refining park and to increase the utilization factor (FUT) of the plants in order to reduce dependence on fuel imports.

In parallel, the current president abandoned the fuel pricing policy based on the so‑called import parity price (PPI) and adopted a methodology that also began to incorporate domestic market references, with the aim of reducing consumers’ exposure to the volatility of barrel prices and the exchange rate.

P-79 is the eighth platform in the Búzios field, located in the pre-salt layer of the Santos Basin

Petrobras reported net income of R$ 52.4 billion (US$ 10.4 billion) in the second quarter of 2026, 97% higher than in the same period of 2025. Adjusted EBITDA amounted to R$ 93.8 billion (US$ 18.6 billion). The company's operational performance drove the financial results for the quarter, which was marked by record levels of Petrobras-operated oil production in Brazil, reaching 2.7 million barrels per day, 15% higher than in the second quarter of 2025, and by record refinery utilisation, with a Refinery Utilisation Factor (RUF) of 101%, increasing the supply of petroleum products to the domestic market. Operating cash flow (OCF) reached R$ 61.8 billion (US$ 12.3 billion), representing a 46% increase over the previous 12 months.
Click here to access the full Petrobras' 2Q26 Financial Performance Report

The increase in oil production supported export growth during the quarter, with exports reaching nearly one million barrels per day. Meanwhile, the high refinery utilisation rate resulted in record production levels during the period, including 509 thousand bpd of S10 diesel and 109 thousand bpd of jet fuel. Petroleum product output reached 1.9 million bpd, representing a 5.6% increase compared with the first quarter of 2026. During a period of volatility in the international market, this increase in petroleum product production contributed to a 40% reduction in imports compared with the previous quarter.

"The operational records we achieved in the second quarter led us to one of the highest quarterly financial results in Petrobras' history. The increase in oil and petroleum product output, combined with higher Brent prices, strengthened our cash generation," said Fernando Melgarejo, Chief Financial Officer and Investor Relations Officer.
